description: Bounded in-memory stream simulation comparing watermark-based tumbling-window aggregation with late-event correction against a naive drop-late baseline, reporting window MAE and late-recovery rate.
method: Generate n_samples events as (event_time, arrival_time, value); ~15% are late (arrival_time > event_time + allowed_lateness). Algorithm: sort by arrival_time, advance watermark = max_event_time_seen - allowed_lateness; on-time events add to their window sum; late events enter a correction buffer applied after the stream ends. Baseline: identical arrival-order processing but late events are silently dropped. Ground truth: assign every event to floor(event_time / window_size) and sum per window. Metrics (lower is better): window_mae = mean of |computed_window_sum - true_window_sum| across all windows. Metrics (higher is better, range [0,1]): late_recovery_rate = fraction of late events correctly included in their window; on_time_accuracy = fraction of non-late events correctly included. No leakage: watermark uses only previously observed arrivals.
category: Real-time data processing: bounded in-memory stream, windowing and late events
